explanations.answer: Each division took its own month
explanations.explanation: That's the schedule, baker. The divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year, and each one had 24,000 men (1 Chronicles 27:1). Twelve divisions, twelve months, and everybody knew when their turn came. I wish my kitchen ran that smooth. My oven schedule is basically vibes.

explanations.answer: Every division served all year long
explanations.explanation: Close, but that would be one tired army. The text says the divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year (1 Chronicles 27:1). So each division took one month, and then the next one stepped in. Nobody had to stand watch for all twelve months straight. Even I take a break from stamping, and I'm made of metal.

explanations.answer: Each division served only in wartime
explanations.explanation: Good guess, but the list doesn't say that. It says the divisions were on rotating military duty each month throughout the year (1 Chronicles 27:1). The text doesn't mention wartime here at all. It just gives a steady schedule, one division for each month.

That's the group. "David did not count the men aged twenty or under…" (1 Chronicles 27:23). So the census had a line drawn right there at twenty. The text gives us that one group and nothing more, so I'm not going to make up extra rules for it.

explanations.answer: Men over the age of sixty
explanations.explanation: Nope, the older men weren't the ones left out. The text says David did not count the men aged twenty or under (1 Chronicles 27:23). The cutoff was on the young end. Sixty never comes up in this passage at all.

Not quite, baker. The ones left out were on the young side. "David did not count the men aged twenty or under…" (1 Chronicles 27:23). Fifty doesn't show up anywhere in this count, so you can set that number down.

explanations.answer: The LORD said Israel would be as many as the stars
explanations.explanation: Right on the money. The text says David left them out "because the LORD had said that He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky." (1 Chronicles 27:23). The reason comes straight from the text, so I don't have to guess. Funny thing, I know a little about stars myself, since mine light up every time a cookie box is sealed.

explanations.answer: The LORD said only older men would go to battle
explanations.explanation: That's a believable one, but the text doesn't say it. The reason given is that the LORD had said He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky (1 Chronicles 27:23). Nothing there is about who goes to battle. When the Bible gives the reason, I'll take the Bible's reason every time.

explanations.answer: The army leaders said they already had plenty of men
explanations.explanation: Nice try, but the army leaders aren't the ones named here. The text says the reason was that the LORD had said He would make Israel as numerous as the stars of the sky (1 Chronicles 27:23). It's tied to what the LORD said. Plenty of men is a fine problem to have, but it isn't the reason given.
